title: Pictures that show what is said
statement: A picture should show what the voice is saying.
example: Mine did for 12 of 22 lines; every miss was structural (a definition, a list, the setting, a rank), and a labelled plate fixed each one.
detail:
Finding 3 of the film study (`othello-unit-video/research/FINDINGS.md`): my paintings showed what the narration said
for 12 of 22 lines; all 10 misses were structural (definitions, lists, the setting, the ranks), and labelled plates
fixed every one.
against:
two visual styles can feel like two films, plates put text on screen for half the runtime, a
plate that teaches a fact can give away the next answer, and I judged the plates myself. A later run found counter-evidence (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`).

Do not hide static slides behind a video-complete label: use progressive spatial/relational diagrams that teach exactly what is said.
If the narration explains the significance of every detail and the pictures merely repeat it, it still misses your point.
Recommend reordering this scene's captions to narration order in a content revision.

On top of that structure, the two most concrete teaching claims in the script are simply not on screen: the "five-part shape" (hero, departure, trial, choice, return) is never visualised or labelled at any point, and of the two monsters named at 51.76s the witch and sirens never appear at all while the "one-eyed giant" is drawn as a cheerful, human-sized man waving hello.
